title: Ethiopian Shiro Sambusa
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Shiro Sambusa — the crispy sambusa pastry filled with thick shiro paste, onion, garlic, and coriander. The fasting-period sambusa — when lentils run out, shiro provides the filling. Silkier and richer than lentil sambusa.
longDesc: Shiro Sambusa uses the chickpea flour stew (shiro) as its filling — the thick shiro sets firmly when cooled, making it an ideal sambusa filling. The resulting sambusa is silkier than lentil-filled versions.
steps: Make thick shiro: cook onion, add shiro powder mixed with water. Cook until very thick. Cool completely.
Shape, fill with thick cool shiro, seal, and fry as per ETH161.
chefTips: Shiro filling must be very thick — it sets as it cools.
commonMistakes: Thin shiro — runs out of the pastry.
cookingScience: See ETH161 for sambusa frying science.
sustainabilityTips: Shiro filling is entirely vegan and fasting-compatible.
culturalNote: Shiro Sambusa is the fasting chef's ingenuity — taking the pantry staple (shiro powder) and using it as a sambusa filling, demonstrating that the Ethiopian fasting tradition produces creative solutions rather than limitations.
